fit.message: CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL

continued_refits.note: The new-site level is what the projection uses and is pinned down; the level at a zero center effect moves along a ridge between the type level, the size trend and the spread of center effects, which the projection does not use.

hidden_cells.note: Each center's hidden sum is fixed by Table 4, so placing the censored cells cannot change the national total. They hold hidden_patients_pct_of_center_totals of patients; where they go changes ZIP counts.

not_patients.note: sum over ZIPs of low-income residents minus low-income patients, floored at 0 in each ZIP

low_income_residents_minus_patients.note: national difference with no flooring; the floored sum is larger by the patients who live in ZIPs where they exceed residents

projection.capacity_is_an_input: The model gives who a site's patients would be, not how many. Patients = the capacity chosen.

rules.served_by_three_centers: urban ZIP, 5,000 to 15,000 low-income residents, exactly three centers with 100+ patients; closest to the median size
rules.no_site_within_20_miles: rural ZIP, 1,500+ low-income residents, no permanent site within 20 miles, penetration under 10%; the largest

A.note: Censored cells hold hidden_patients_pct_of_center_totals of patients. Where they are placed changes ZIP counts, not the national total. The fitted expectation places small cells worse than an equal split, so a flat prior with the exact center sums is used; the interval for one placed cell is nearly the whole 1 to 15 range.

B.note: The negative-binomial 80% intervals cover well above 80% of held-out cells, so they are wider than needed, not calibrated. Poisson-only intervals cover far less. The fit uses a Poisson likelihood, so intervals on new-site numbers reflect parameter uncertainty only; interval_80_coverage_poisson_only shows how much the Poisson noise model understates spread.

D.note: Sites added in the first half of 2025 serve part of the 2025 reporting year only; the exposure-scaled rows multiply each prediction by the share of the year in scope, and the model still runs high. Sites that closed are missing from HRSA's October 2026 list, which also shifts the competition around the 2025 additions.

E.note: HRSA's published penetration is computed from the same UDS patients-by-ZIP table, so agreement checks our ZIP-to-ZCTA joins, the crosswalk and the denominators. It does not check the model. Our low-income penetration sits below HRSA's by about the income share we apply to patients (median_ratio_ours_to_hrsa); HRSA does not scale its numerator.

cannot_answer: where a new site's patients come from

workbook_vs_python.note: Workbook formulas recalculated in LibreOffice. Patient counts are shown only where the capacity is 5,000 or less and a typical site there draws more than 5,000 (site_capacity_binds = 1), where they equal the page's min(draw, capacity) times the new share; elsewhere only the shares show. The workbook, the ZIP table and the page use the same 24 of the 100 parameter sets; the remaining difference is the page data's rounding.

definitions.low_income: under 200% of the federal poverty level (ACS table C17002, estimates 002 to 007)
definitions.patients_low_income: a center's patients in a ZIP times that center's share at or below 200% of poverty (Table 4 lines 1 to 3 over lines 1 to 4, unknown excluded); assumes a center's ZIP mix equals its overall mix
definitions.penetration: low-income patients of all centers over low-income residents; ours, not HRSA's (HRSA's published value is a comparator)
definitions.not_patients: low-income residents minus low-income patients, floored at 0; one measure, they may use other care
definitions.under_10_and_25_pct: our own thresholds on penetration, named as ours on the page; not an HRSA rule
definitions.small_zip: under 1,000 low-income residents: ACS margins are wide; left out of ranks and ranked tables, counted in totals
definitions.campus_zip: college and graduate students (ACS B14001) are 20% or more of residents aged 3 and over. The poverty count includes students living off campus, so these ZIPs look poorer and less reached than their non-student residents; left out of ranks and ranked tables, counted in totals
definitions.typical_site: a single new site with the median attractiveness of its type (center type effect at one site)
definitions.draw: model quantity behind patients = min(capacity, draw). Not published: most single sites would exceed any plausible capacity, so capacity is an input and the projection gives shares (new, from neighbours, payer mix)
definitions.interval: reach figures: 10th to 90th percentile over Monte Carlo draws of the ACS margins and of the censored cells (2,000 draws). New-site shares: over 24 of the 100 bootstrap refits of the model. Survey and parameter uncertainty only: yearly patient-count noise and the assumptions in 'limits' are not in it
definitions.tile_3: mean over 226 held-out centers of the share of a center's patients living in the 20 ZIPs the model ranked highest for it; patient_weighted weights centers by size. Baselines: the 20 nearest ZIPs and the 20 ZIPs with most low-income residents
definitions.geography: 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa and Northern Mariana patients are in Table 4 totals but in no ZIP table
definitions.new_patients: patients who, in the model, use no health center today (the outside option); the rest of a site's patients are taken from neighbouring centers

limits: 'Other ZIP Codes' lines hold 668,157 patients (2.0% of all patients, 3.5% of the average center and up to 51% of one). They cannot be placed on a ZIP, so they are in no ZIP's count.
Look-alike centers (170 modeled as competitors) have no patients in the UDS awardee file. Their patients are not counted, so they show as people not reached.
A person served by two centers is counted twice: UDS patients are unduplicated within a center only.

Supply is permanent, non-school sites. The site list has 2,475 seasonal rows, 1,419 mobile van rows and 4,831 rows in a school setting that are left out. A mobile unit or outreach team is not in the supply.
ACS counts college students as low-income, which lifts the counts of some ZIPs near campuses.
Distance is straight-line miles to the center's nearest permanent site. Drive time, transit and borders are not in it.
Patients' income is each center's overall low-income share applied to every ZIP of that center. Without that scaling the residents in ZIPs under 25% reached fall by 3.7 million.
The thresholds of 10% and 25% penetration are ours, not an HRSA rule.
Sites that closed are missing from the October 2026 site list, which shifts the competition around the 2025 openings.

Intervals are parameter and survey uncertainty. Yearly patient-count noise, the capacity and who could use a center are not in them: the median share of a site's patients with no center today is 0.65 with low-income residents as the market and 0.90 with all residents.
